subject: Post-call recap: telemetry sanitization, trace-id handling & demo plan
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Jane Ellis <jane.ellis@carebridge.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 2 Sep 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: telemetry sanitization, trace-id handling & demo plan

Jane — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick written recap and proposed next steps so nothing falls through the cracks.

Call highlights (technical + compliance asks):
- CareBridge will treat request/response audit logs as potentially PHI; you need: residency in us-east-1, trace-id masking, and a retention policy we discussed.
- Primary telemetry of concern: headers (Authorization, X-Trace-ID), request/response bodies (occasionally include identifiers), and post-call cookies.
- Desired outcome: capability to ingest logs for troubleshooting while ensuring sensitive values are either redacted or irreversibly hashed and traceability for short window only.

Notes / suggestions from our side:
- Dual approach for headers: (a) suppress highly-sensitive headers at the edge, (b) hash/pepper X-Trace-ID at ingestion for short-term correlation. Hashing should be HMAC-SHA256 with a customer-managed key (KMS) where possible.
- Example trace header we see in sample logs:
  X-Trace-ID: 123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174000
  Proposal: replace with trace-id: <hashed(123e4567...)> and store mapping in an ephemeral lookup that expires after 30 days.
- Retention options: pilot customers often pick 30 days (default), 90 days (extended), or 365 days (rare, requires legal OK).
- For request/response bodies: we can plug in a lightweight rule-based scrubbing engine to remove obvious PII (emails, SSNs, phone numbers) and send a sanitized copy to the audit store.

Action items (proposed):
1) Technical pilot: we provision a short-lived test endpoint and ingest a small set of redacted logs you provide (2 weeks). Markus/Karthik to run the pilot.
2) Security evidence: we provide SOC2 in-scope attestations and a short summary of our KMS approach (Markus to share).
3) Residency & procurement: connect our sales ops with Tom Rivera to begin paperwork and confirm VPC/network requirements.

Proposed demo slots (30–45m):
- Fri 2026-09-04 09:00–09:45 PT
- Mon 2026-09-07 11:00–11:45 PT
Please pick one that works for you and we'll send an invite.

Attachments: I attached a small sample log excerpt (carebridge-sample-logs.txt) and a short PDF with three redaction patterns we recommend (redaction-options.pdf).

If you want, we can also share a one-page summary for your legal team describing the ephemeral mapping strategy.

Thanks —
Markus
Markus Klein

Subject: Re: Post-call recap: telemetry sanitization, trace-id handling & demo plan

Markus — appreciate the concise summary, that matches our notes. A few clarifications from the privacy team: 

1) For trace IDs we prefer irreversible hashing (HMAC with a customer key) over reversible mapping. We need the ability to correlate an incident for 30 days only.
2) Key management: if you can integrate with our AWS KMS CMK (we can provide a cross-account role) that's preferred; otherwise we need details on your KMS rotation policy.
3) Residency: all logs for this pilot will live in us-east-1 and must not replicate outside that region.
4) Retention: start with 30 days for the pilot; we may evaluate 90 days if legal signs off.

I attached our privacy questionnaire (carebridge-privacy-questionnaire.pdf) — legal asked for a couple items around deletion verification and access logs.

We can do the demo Friday 09/04 at 09:00 PT. Tom (procurement) will join the demo to get a sense of the commercial steps.

Thanks —
Jane Ellis
Director, Engineering Operations | CareBridge Health
jane.ellis@carebridge.com | +1 (212) 555-0142

Subject: Re: Post-call recap: telemetry sanitization, trace-id handling & demo plan

Great — confirmed for Fri 09/04 09:00 PT. Short update + proposed internal owners and timeline so we stay coordinated: 

Owners: 
- Technical pilot & demo: Karthik Iyer (karthik.iyer@redwood.com)
- Security evidence & privacy questionnaire responses: Monica Patel (monica.patel@redwood.com)
- Commercial / procurement: Markus (me) to loop in Sales Ops after the demo

Planned two-week pilot outline (high-level):
1) Day 0–2: ingest 100–200 sample log lines into a staging bucket in us-east-1 (we will not replicate).
2) Day 3–7: apply header suppression & hashing rules; run automated scrubber across request bodies and generate sanitized audit store.
3) Day 8–12: access controls review + evidence handover (Monica will prepare deletion proof and access logs).
4) Day 13–14: wrap-up demo of runbooks & handoff to your on-call.

We will integrate with an AWS KMS CMK if you provide the cross-account role — Karthik, please prepare the short KMS integration doc to share during the demo.

Next steps before demo: 
- Tom: if procurement can start a standard MSA route, I can send a DocuSign powerform to speed signature. DocuSign link: https://www.docusign.net/Member/PowerFormSigning.aspx?PowerFormId=abcd-1234
- Jane: please upload the privacy questionnaire to the HubSpot record (I linked it here) so Monica can track outstanding items: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/contact/7890

If that all sounds good, we'll use the demo to run a quick end-to-end ingest and show the hashed trace-id behavior (no PHI in the demo samples).

Thanks and see you Friday —
Markus

Quick internal note — tested the lightweight scrubbing pipeline against the sample logs Markus dropped: hashing X-Trace-ID (HMAC-SHA256) + edge header suppression adds ~8ms median to the ingest path in staging (well within SLO). No blockers on KMS integration. Willbring the short KMS integration doc for the demo.

— Karthik
